[prose] All landscape metrics included in the model selec tion were centered to zero using the standardize function in the vegan package due to the range of absolute values that varied naturally. In order to access the complexity of the relationships between landscape structure, bee species, and functional diversity, we compared the multiple competing hypotheses using model selection analysis and a selection criterion corrected for small sample sizes (Akaike Information Criterion—AICc). The analysis also provides the difference between the AICc value of a given model and the most parsimonious model (ΔAICc), as well as the weight of evidence $( w _ { i } )$ of each model. Cuckoo bees depend on the presence of their host and the resources it provides (Rozen 2001; Michener 2007), meaning that they are directly affected by landscape disturbances. Thus, a linear response to environmental metrics can be attenuated in some circumstances. A pair of long-term studies by Martins et al. (2013) and Cardoso and Gonçalves (2018) monitored Sites 10 and 3, respectively, and did not find evidence of declines in kleptoparasites. As discussed by Sheffield et al. (2013), kleptoparasites can be indicative of the status of the total bee assemblage and, as expected, they were more affected by the metrics evaluated than the bee community at large (assumed by the higher intercept values), indicating that monitoring in urban areas should also focus on these bees.

[prose] A recent review on the importance of multi-scale studies underscored the ability of some factors to impair analysis (Miguet et al. 2016), especially the decreasing of variance values as the scale increases. We did not find a relevant decrease from 750 to 2 km, and the landscape diversity variance increased instead (Online Resource 9). The smaller buffer (750 m) had the greatest degree of explanatory power for our data, suggesting that nearby resources and nesting substrate are important, both in Curitiba and other cities
